title: Shell lace prayer shawl
subtitle: A wide, comforting shawl in dk weight shell lace, beginner-friendly.
excerpt: A prayer shawl in shell lace is wide, warm, and simple to make. This dk weight version uses a four-row shell repeat that is easy to memorise. The finished shawl wraps around the shoulders with plenty of fabric to spare.
sourceNotes: Shell lace is one of the oldest crochet stitch families, documented in Weldon's Practical Crochet (1880s) and Priscilla Crochet publications (early 1900s, Internet Archive). Prayer shawl knitting and crochet became a popular charity and spiritual practice from the 1990s onward. This pattern is original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: Five (or more) trebles worked into the same stitch or chain space, fanning out to form a fan or shell shape.
The full unit of one shell and its surrounding stitches that tiles across the row to build the fabric.
A single double crochet worked into the chain space between two shells to hold the fabric flat and set the position for the next row's shell.

crochet.gaugeText: 1 shell (5 tr) + 1 dc = 4.5 cm wide in dk weight with a 4 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: One size, 180 cm x 70 cm, unblocked.

content.text: A shell lace prayer shawl is 180 cm long and 70 cm wide, worked flat in rows. The
is four rows that are easy to remember after the first few: shell into chain space,
into shell centre, and back again. DK weight on a 4 mm hook gives a warm, drapy fabric.

itself is five trebles into one space. It fans out from a narrow base to a wide top and the shells stack on top of each other row by row, anchored in between by single double crochets. The rhythm is satisfying and meditative once established.

items.name: DK weight yarn
items.substitutions: Any soft DK in a wool-acrylic or bamboo blend works. Avoid very textured yarns as they hide the shell definition.

content.text: 1 shell (5 tr) + 1 dc = 4.5 cm wide in dk weight with a 4 mm hook. The row height is about 4 cm per two-row repeat. Work one shell repeat and measure before starting. At 4.5 cm per repeat, the shawl needs 40 shell repeats to reach 180 cm.
: 1 dc into centre tr of shell below
Ch 183. Foundation row (wrong side): 1 dc into 4th ch from hook. *Skip 2 ch, 5 tr (shell) into next ch, skip 2 ch, 1 dc into next ch.* Repeat from * to * across. Turn. (40 shells.)

Ch 3 (counts as 1 tr). 2 tr into first dc (half shell at edge). *1 dc into centre tr of next shell, 5 tr (shell) into next dc.* Repeat to last shell. 1 dc into centre tr of last shell. 3 tr into last dc (half shell at edge). Turn.
Ch 1. 1 dc into first tr. *5 tr (shell) into next dc, 1 dc into centre tr of next shell.* Repeat across. End with 1 dc into top of turning ch. Turn.
Repeat Rows 1 and 2 until the shawl measures 180 cm. Fasten off and weave in all ends.
Work one row of dc (UK) along each short end: pick up one dc per row end, working into the side of each row. Fasten off. This gives the short ends a firm, even edge.
Follow the yarn label. Most DK wool-acrylic blends are machine washable on a gentle 30-degree cycle. Lay flat to dry to preserve the shell shapes. Do not tumble dry.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: Shell lace shawls have a few straightforward issues.

items.cause: Not working into the correct anchor points
items.fix: The dc always goes into the centre (3rd) treble of the shell below. The shell always goes into the dc between two shells. Count 5 trebles per shell before moving to the next dc.

items.cause: Half shells at the edges not counted correctly
items.fix: The half shells at each end (3 tr into the edge stitch) replace a full shell at the corner. If you see the fabric widening, remove the extra trebles from the edge half shells.

items.cause: Turning chain height not matching shell
items.fix: The ch-3 turning chain counts as the first treble. Work 2 tr more into the same base stitch to complete the edge half shell and match the height of the shells across the row.
